test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-6) Official paper (Held On: 9 May 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Out of a total sum of ₹5,000, Danish invested one part at 12% simple interest per annum and the remaining part at 10% simple interest per annum. If the total interest that accrued to Danish in two years equals ₹1072, what was the sum Danish invested at 12% simple interest per annum?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the entire ₹5,000 was invested at 10%, the interest for 2 years would be = (5000 × 10 × 2) ÷ 100 = ₹1,000.

Actual interest accrued is ₹1,072, which is an extra 1072 − 1000 = ₹72.

This extra ₹72 is generated because the first part was invested at an extra 2% (12% − 10%) for 2 years.

∴ 2% of Sum₁ × 2 = ₹72 ⇒ 4% of Sum₁ = ₹72

⇒ Sum₁ = 72 × (100 ÷ 4) = ₹1,800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Principal = ₹5,000

Rate₁ = 12% p.a., Rate₂ = 10% p.a.

Total Time = 2 years

Total Simple Interest = ₹1,072

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100
